20-01-opti-1: Tick, tock. A plant can never walk away.
20-01-opti-2: In Fort Myers, Florida, one giant tree spreads out like a whole forest.
20-01-opti-3: Look up. Long roots hang down from its branches.
20-01-opti-5: They grow down until they touch the ground. Then they become new trunks.
20-01-opti-6: Now tip a young plant on its side. What will it do?
20-01-opti-7: Its stems curve back up, toward the sky.
20-01-opti-8: Plants can't move. So how do they know which way to grow?
20-01-welcome: Today's film starts with a giant tree in Florida. First, look closely at a plant whose stems fell over.
20-01-lesson: Today you're the plant detective. Test light and water in the Stem and Root Lab, then find out what each plant was responding to.
20-01-assign: Time to show what you know about how plants respond to light.
20-01-words: Response. Environment. Stimulus. Gravity. Phototropism. Survival. Gravitropism. Hydrotropism.
how-20-01-compare: Put the desk lamp beside one tray and the wet sponge beside the other: drag them, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Let three days pass. Then swap them and press it again.
how-20-01-partc: Draw a plant in a pot near a sunny window, after it has responded. Label the stem, two leaves, the roots, and the light. Add an arrow that shows how the plant responded.
how-20-01-write: A plant is growing in a corner with light coming from only one side. Explain what will happen to this plant over the next few weeks. Use at least one of the science words under the boxes.
20-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
